findings: BeginCombat and first IssueCombatOrders returned before stall: report combatOrderRounds=1 and resource sample at combat+0.0044651 seconds. No missile-shot or casualty callback had occurred.

Ranged-only changes are stock bow/arrow fixed equipment, opposing fronts at +/-45 units, Ranged formations, Stop order and FireAtWill. Common activation sets teams hostile, all owned AI Alarmed and valid live target indices.

Stock Formation.SetFiringOrder invokes Agent.SetFiringOrder. Native SetFiringOrder compares existing enum and returns unchanged when equal; duplicate formation and individual FireAtWill is not a repeated state reset.
Native SetTargetAgent writes a valid target index to Agent AI+0x140 and sets flag0x40; managed caller accepts a live opposite-side Agent. No invalid/null/overflow index found in harness construction.
Stalled worker path is Human_anim_system::virtual-slot8 (64f860), direct helper6520c0 then6dffc0. Exact call instructions650ca5/653421 account for stack return addresses650caa/653426.
Only caller-body native patch is653406 relocated Mission field; no caller control flow or order setter is altered by candidate.

Simultaneously waking all4080 archers is intentional maximum workload and can expose an independent animation auxiliary-buffer capacity. Suppressing orders or reducing count would hide rather than establish a fix.

REA6520c0 confirms final helper6dffc0 is called with Human_anim_system+45f0 auxiliary object when nonnull and animation flags25f4 or25f5 are set, provided current Mission byte1044844 is zero; native code independently matches these guards. This is an animation update/auxiliary submission path; exact auxiliary class name remains unproved.
unknowns: This review does not prove every native AI/animation invariant; allocator ownership/capacity root cause and fix belong to separate review.
No claim that target pairing or Stop order causes the native buffer overflow; exact causal trace requires allocator/consumer proof.
recommendedAction: Keep managed workload frozen. Finish independent auxiliary-buffer capacity/lifecycle fix and exact tests; rerun unchanged ranged workload only after parent runtime gates.

limitations: The session serves operations only after Ghidra reports default auto-analysis complete; incomplete analysis does not expose partial results.
The imported Program and temporary project are ephemeral and deleted on close. Annotation operations edit session database metadata; original executable bytes are never written.
Cancelling an active Ghidra request terminates its ephemeral database and discards session annotations. The selected target remains open; the next provider query imports the original artifact again.
Default-space addresses use lowercase 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; other address spaces use <percent-encoded-space>:0x<hex>.
Pseudocode is Ghidra decompiler output, not original source and not text-equivalent to Hopper output.
External functions and functions without an analyzable body return null; other decompiler failures remain explicit.
Windows Ghidra P0 accepts native x86 and x86-64 PE applications and DLLs, and explicitly selected raw 6502 images; managed, hostile, sensitive, and mutable-path targets are unsupported.
The Windows bridge uses authenticated IPv4 loopback because Node path-based IPC does not expose Java AF_UNIX sockets; the endpoint file contains no bearer token.

Windows sessions require the matching packaged Windows x64 native addon, local NTFS targets and runtimes, and Windows 10 or later. Native handles enforce path admission, private DACLs, and Job Object ownership automatically.

The target references PDB TaleWorlds.Native.pdb (GUID 2029ba6e-176d-498a-903c-b56d1af1370c, age (hex) 1, signature unknown, version RSDS); Ghidra reports load state unknown. Original names and types may be missing; an empty name search does not prove a procedure is absent. Use list_procedures and address-based analysis to inspect recovered functions.
